title: WPSS/449/2018 of Arvind Kumar Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No.449 of 2018 (S/S)

State of Uttarakhand & Ors. ....Respondents
Mr. Shobhit Saharia, Advocate for the petitioner
Mrs. Seema Sah, Brief Holder for the State
Hon'ble Lok Pal Singh, J.

Petitioner has approached this Court seeking
the following reliefs:-
i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of certiorari for quashing the order
dated 15.12.2017 issued by the
Uttarakhand Police Headquarter, whereby
the representation submitted by the
petitioner for treating the categorization of
the petitioner ACR entry 'Excellent' for the
year 2010 to be 'Outstanding' as per the
Govt. Orders has been rejected in a cryptic
manner and also quash the
communication dated 8th August 2017.
ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of certiorari for quashing the
selection and appointment of the private
respondent no.4 on the post of Inspector
(Civil Police) vide order dated 15th October
2016 issued by the Office of the Director
General, Uttarakhand Police
Headquarters, Dehradun.
iii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus commanding and
directing the respondents to award 1.5
additional marks for the entry Excellent

2
given to the petitioner for the year 2010
treating the same to be "outstanding" in
the selection process for the post of
Inspector (Civil Police) and accordingly
revise the marks allotted to the petitioner
on the basis of service record.
iv) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus commanding and
directing the respondents to consider the
candidature of the petitioner for promotion
on the post of Inspector (Civil Police) after
revising the marks of the petitioner, in the
selection process initiated in the year
2015 for the said post.
2. Factual matrix of the case is that on
02.02.2015 the Police Headquarters issued a Circular
for making regular selection on the post of Inspector
(Civil Police) from Sub Inspector (Civil Police) who has
completed minimum 10 years of service on the post of
Sub Inspector and have satisfactory service record
from 01.01.2004. Appointment by promotion on the
post of Inspector (Civil Police) in Uttarakhand Police is
governed by the procedure prescribed vide Notification
dated 23.09.2004 notified by the Department of Home,
Government of Uttarakhand, which contemplates that
for promotion on the post of Inspector (Civil
Police/Intelligence), the Sub Inspector (Civil
Police/Intelligence) who have rendered at least 10
years of service as such on 1st day of April of a
recruitment year and have satisfactory service record of
10 years will be eligible. This Notification was
subsequently amended by another Notification dated
15.09.2006 whereby clause 3 of the Notification was
amended by providing that 35 marks would be

3
available for ACR entries. It was further clarified that
for awarding the marks based on ACR entries of last 5
years, 3.5 marks would be awarded for 'Outstanding'
category, 02 marks for 'Very Good' and 01 marks for
'Good'. On 18.12.2003, the State Government issued a
Government Order regarding the procedure for ACR
entries which provided that at the end of the ACR
entry, the reporting officer would provided the grading
of concerned employee based on his total work and
conduct. The grading would be categorized as
Outstanding, Very Good, Good, satisfactory and
bad/unsatisfactory. Subsequently, the State
Government issued another Government Order dated
30.09.2010 providing that ACR entries would be
categorized in 04 categories viz. Outstanding, Very
Good, Good, Bad/Unsatisfactory, which was, however,
repealed/cancelled vide another Government Order
dated 10.12.2012 and the government order dated
18.12.2003 was revoked which provided that the ACR
entries would be graded in 05 categories, namely,
Outstanding, Very Good, Good, satisfactory and
bad/unsatisfactory.
3. On 07.10.2016, the Office of the Director
General of Police, Uttarakhand issued a Circular
regarding holding of the Interview for selection on the
post of Inspector (Civil Police), which provided that the
selection has to be held for promotion against 126
vacancies on the post of Inspector (Civil Police) and
candidates four times of the vacancies i.e. 230 eligible
Sub Inspector would be called for interview. Petitioner,
being eligible, was also included in the list of eligible
Sub Inspector to be called for interview. Merit list was
prepared on the basis of marks obtained in ACR

4
entries and interview, which showed that the last
promotee Inspector (Civil Police) has obtained 74.5
marks out of 100 whereas the petitioner has secured
73.5 marks. Vide order dated 15.10.2016 and
03.05.2017, total 124 Sub Inspectors (Civil Police),
excluding the petitioner, have been promoted on the
post of Inspector (Civil Police and Intelligence).
Petitioner obtained information under the Right to
Information Act and came to know that for the ACR
entry 'Excellent' for the year 2010 the petitioner has
been awarded 02 marks. Thereafter, the petitioner
made a representation to the Director General of Police,
Uttarakhand, Dehradun, in respect of grading of the
ACR entry awarded in the year 2010 to the petitioner
as 'Excellent' being contrary to the provisions of the
Government Orders in force pertaining to the recording
of the ACR entries, and requested that the ACR entry of
the petitioner for the year 2010 be treated as
'Outstanding' in place of 'Excellent'. Representation of
the petitioner was rejected by the Police Department by
order dated 15.12.2017.
4. It is the contention of learned counsel for the
petitioner that the as per the Government Order which
was in force at the relevant point of time, the ACR
entries were to be categorized as Outstanding, Very
Good, Good, Bad/Unsatisfactory, there was no such
category as 'Excellent', therefore, the category
'Excellent' awarded to the petitioner for the year 2010
is contrary to the said Government Order. It is also the
contention that the respondents have wrongly given 02
marks for the ACR entry by treating the category
'Excellent' as equivalent to 'Very Good'. According to
the petitioner, 'Excellent' is equivalent to 'Outstanding'

5
and thus he has to be awarded 3.5 marks, and as
such, the petitioner secured 75 marks.
5. Counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of
respondent no.2, wherein it is stated as per the
government order no.1712/Karmik-2/2003 dated
18.12.2003 regarding the annual entries the following
categories has been fixed:-
1. Outstanding 2. Very Good 3. Good. 4. Satisfactory 5.
Bad/Unsatisfactory.
 It is also stated that in the ACR of the petitioner
for the year 2010 word 'Excellent' has been mentioned,
which has been treated/evaluated as Very Good and
the petitioner has been given 02 marks for the same
which is correct as per law. It is also stated that in the
ACR entry of the petitioner for the year 2010 the word
'Excellent' has been mentioned as per the government
order issued by the State of U.P. dated 23.03.1994,
which provides that entry 'Excellent' be calculated as
'very good'.
6. Rejoinder affidavit has also been filed by the
petitioner denying the averments made in the counter
affidavit.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties
and have gone through the entire material available on
record.
8. Although a detailed counter affidavit has
been filed by the respondent no.2 but the same is
evasive and vague. In the counter affidavit, on the one
hand the respondents states that the State
Government has issued government orders from time

6
to time regarding ACR entries and that as per
Government Order dated 18.12.2003 it was directed
that the ACR entries would be graded in 05 categories,
namely, Outstanding, Very Good, Good, satisfactory
and bad/unsatisfactory, while on the other hand the
respondents states that the petitioner has been given
category 'Excellent' in his ACR, which as per
Government Order dated 23.03.1994, issued by the
State of U.P., is equivalent to 'Very Good'. After the
creation of State of Uttarakhand, when a specific
government order has been issued by the Government
of Uttarakhand, in regard to ACR entries, the
Government Order dated 23.03.1994 issued by the
State of U.P. before bifurcation, would become
redundant for the State of Uttarakhand.
9. The Government Order dated 18.12.2003
issued by the Government of Uttarakhand provided
that the ACR entries would be graded in 05 categories,
namely, Outstanding, Very Good, Good, satisfactory
and bad/unsatisfactory. However, the petitioner has
been awarded 'Excellent'. In the ACR of the petitioner,
it has been recorded that he is 'Hardworking and
sincere Sub Inspector has been categorized as
'Excellent'. 'Excellent' does not find mention in the
government order dated 18.12.2003, but due to
ignorance of the reporting officer, petitioner has been
awarded entry 'Excellent', which according to the
respondents is equivalent to 'Very Good' and on such
basis petitioner has been awarded 02 marks for the
ACR entry for the year 2010. As per the Oxford
Dictionary, the meaning of word 'Excellent' is an
adjective which means very great, outstanding; the
meaning of Outstanding is exceptionally good, clearly

7
noticeable, not yet done or paid. The words
'Outstanding' and 'Excellent' connote one and the same
meaning which is distinct from the word 'Very Good'.
10. In the light of aforesaid, this Court is of the
considered view that firstly the reporting officer has
committed error in awarding the petitioner entry
'Excellent' which was contrary to the Government
Orders and secondly the respondents have further
committed mistake in treating the ACR entry 'Excellent'
equivalent to 'Very Good' and thereby awarding 02
marks to the petitioner. Petitioner cannot be made to
suffer on account of mistake committed by the
reporting officer.
11. Accordingly, writ petition is allowed. A writ
of mandamus is issued against the respondent
Department with the following directions:-
i) ACR entry of the petitioner for the year 2010
wherein entry of 'Excellent' has been awarded
shall be treated as 'Outstanding' by the
respondent department and 1.5 additional
marks shall be awarded to the petitioner in the
selection process, and thereafter, the petitioner
shall be declared successful for promotion on
the post of Inspector (Civil Police).
ii) As by changing the nomenclature of the ACR
entry from 'Excellent' to 'Outstanding, the
petitioner has now secured 75 marks, he shall
be treated to be promoted on the post of
Inspector (Civil Police) from the date when the
person who has secured 74.5 marks was
promoted.

8
iii) Respondent Department shall accordingly fix
the salary of the petitioner. Arrears of
enhanced salary, by virtue of promotion, shall
be paid to the petitioner within a period of six
months from today.
iv) Seniority of the petitioner shall be fixed as per
the marks secured in the selection process.
11. No order as to costs.
